subject.title: Gateway crash-loops on startup when legacy `plugins/installs.json` conflicts with shared SQLite plugin index (`doctor --fix` does not reconcile)

question: When legacy plugin install metadata conflicts with an internally valid SQLite record, should doctor treat SQLite as authoritative and archive the legacy file, or require explicit operator selection between the two records?
rationale: The migration must converge, but choosing either record can change an intentional plugin source, pin, integrity value, or install path; repository policy establishes SQLite as the runtime store without fully defining conflict arbitration.

options.title: Verify SQLite, archive legacy
options.body: Doctor validates the SQLite record and installed payload, preserves the legacy JSON as a backup, then archives it so startup can proceed.

options.title: Require operator selection
options.body: Doctor presents both records and refuses destructive reconciliation until the operator chooses the authoritative install metadata.

options.title: Make conflict warning-only
options.body: Gateway starts using SQLite while leaving the legacy conflict unresolved for later manual repair.

recommendation.title: Verify SQLite, archive legacy
recommendation.body: Doctor validates the SQLite record and installed payload, preserves the legacy JSON as a backup, then archives it so startup can proceed.
